title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Opinions on Promoting the Reform of the Case Filing Registration System in the People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Opinions on Promoting the Reform of the Case-Filing Registration System in People's Courts

Fa Fa [2015] No. 6

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

On April 1, 2015, the 11th meeting of the Central Leading Group for Comprehensively Deepening Reforms deliberated and adopted the Opinions on Promoting the Reform of the Case-Filing Registration System in People's Courts (hereinafter referred to as the Opinions), which are hereby issued for your earnest implementation. The Opinions shall take effect on May 1, 2015. Please promptly report to the Supreme People's Court any circumstances or issues discovered during implementation.

April 15, 2015

Opinions on Promoting the Reform of the Case-Filing Registration System in People's Courts

In order to fully protect the litigants' right to sue, effectively address the "difficulty in filing cases" that the people have strongly complained about, reform the court's case acceptance system, and change the case-filing review system to a case-filing registration system, the following opinions are put forward in accordance with relevant laws such as the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, and the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC.

1. Guiding Ideology for the Reform of the Case-Filing Registration System

(1) Adhere to the correct political direction. Thoroughly implement the spirit of the Fourth Plenary Session of the 18th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, adhere to the mass line of the Party, adhere to justice for the people and impartial justice, and through the reform of the case-filing registration system, promote the accelerated construction of a fair, efficient, and authoritative socialist judicial system.

(2) Adhere to the Constitution and laws as the basis. Protect the litigants' right to exercise their litigation rights in accordance with the law, facilitate litigation for the parties, and ensure openness, transparency, and efficiency.

(3) Adhere to the principle that cases must be filed and complaints must be heard. For cases that meet the conditions stipulated by law, the court must accept them in accordance with the law, and no unit or individual may obstruct the court from accepting cases under any pretext.

2. Scope of Registration and Case Filing

Cases falling under any of the following circumstances shall be registered and filed:

(1) Civil actions brought by citizens, legal persons, or other organizations with a direct interest in the case, where there is a clear defendant, specific claims and factual basis, and the matter falls within the jurisdiction of the people's court and the court receiving the complaint;

(2) Administrative actions brought by the counterparty of an administrative act, or by citizens, legal persons, or other organizations with an interest in the administrative act, where there is a clear defendant, specific claims and factual basis, and the matter falls within the scope of acceptance of the people's court and the jurisdiction of the court receiving the complaint;

(3) Cases that are handled only upon complaint, minor criminal cases for which the victim has evidence, and cases where the victim has evidence that the criminal suspect should be pursued for criminal responsibility but the public security organs or the People's Procuratorate have not pursued it, and the victim complains, with a clear defendant, specific claims, and evidence proving the criminal facts of the defendant, and the matter falls within the jurisdiction of the court receiving the complaint;

(4) Cases where an effective legal instrument has content for performance, and the subject of enforcement and the person subject to enforcement are clear, and the obligee or his heir or successor in interest files an application within the statutory period, and the matter falls within the jurisdiction of the court receiving the application;

(5) Cases where a compensation claimant files an application with the people's court that is the compensation obligor, or files a compensation application because he is dissatisfied with the compensation or review decision made by the people's court, people's procuratorate, or public security organ, or dissatisfied with inaction beyond the time limit.

Cases falling under any of the following circumstances shall not be registered and filed:

(1) Illegal prosecutions or those that do not meet the statutory conditions for prosecution;

(2) Litigation that has already concluded;

(3) Matters involving harm to national sovereignty and territorial integrity, harm to national security, undermining national unity and ethnic solidarity, or undermining national religious policies;

(4) Other matters that are not within the purview of the people's court.

3. Registration and Case-Filing Procedure

(1) Implement on-the-spot registration and case filing. For complaints, private prosecutions, and applications that meet the requirements of the law, all pleadings shall be accepted and registered and filed on the spot. For those that cannot be determined on the spot whether they meet the requirements of the law, a decision on whether to file the case shall be made within the statutory time limit.

(2) Implement a one-time comprehensive notification and correction. Where the materials for complaints, private prosecutions, and applications do not meet the formal requirements, explanations shall be given promptly, and the materials to be supplemented and the time limit shall be notified comprehensively in writing at one time. If the materials are supplemented within the specified time limit and meet the conditions stipulated by law, the people's court shall register and file the case.

(3) Handling of complaints, private prosecutions, and applications that do not meet legal requirements. For complaints, private prosecutions, and applications that do not meet legal requirements, a ruling shall be made in accordance with the law not to accept the case or not to file the case, stating the reasons. If the party disagrees, an appeal may be filed or an application for reconsideration may be made. It is prohibited to refuse to accept materials, fail to respond, or fail to issue legal instruments.

(4) Strictly implement the standards for case filing. It is prohibited to set acceptance conditions beyond those provided by law, and any "local policies" for case filing that do not comply with the law shall be comprehensively reviewed and abolished.

4. Improve Supporting Mechanisms

(1) Improve the diversified dispute resolution mechanism. Further improve the diversified dispute resolution mechanism that organically connects and coordinates mediation, arbitration, administrative adjudication, administrative reconsideration, and litigation, strengthen the effective connection between pre-litigation mediation and litigation mediation, and provide the people with more dispute resolution methods.

(2) Establish and improve pre-trial preparation procedures. Improve the working mechanisms for sorting complex and simple cases and conducting pre-mediation. Explore the establishment of pre-trial preparation procedures, convene pre-trial conferences, clarify the parties' claims and defenses, summarize the points of dispute, fix relevant evidence, and promote the efficient resolution of disputes through mediation, conciliation, summary judgment, and judgment.

(3) Strengthen case-filing service measures. Strengthen the construction of litigation service centers and information technology in people's courts to achieve open and convenient case filing. Promote online case filing, appointment-based case filing, and circuit case filing to provide convenience for litigants to exercise their right to sue. Increase legal aid and judicial assistance to ensure that parties with genuine financial difficulties can afford to litigate.

5. Sanction Illegal and Abusive Litigation

(1) Legally punish false litigation. Where parties maliciously collude or impersonate others to initiate litigation, attempting to infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of others through litigation, mediation, or other means, the people's court shall dismiss their claims and impose fines or detention; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.

(2) Legally sanction illegal acts. Those who cause disturbances, stay, or storm the courtroom and do not heed the persuasion of judicial personnel; who obstruct judicial personnel from performing their duties by violence, threats, or other methods; or who fabricate facts, insult or slander judicial personnel and seriously disrupt the registration and case-filing work, shall be fined or detained; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.

(3) Legally maintain case-filing order. For illegal acts such as besieging, sitting in protest, pestering and disturbing, storming the court, or otherwise interfering with the lawful case filing by the people's court, the public security organs shall impose penalties such as warnings, fines, or administrative detention in accordance with the Public Security Administration Punishments Law; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.

(4) Improve relevant legal systems. Strengthen the construction of litigation integrity and regulate the exercise of the right to sue. Promote the improvement of relevant legislation, clarify the standards for administrative punishment, judicial punishment, and criminal punishment for acts of abusing the right to sue such as false litigation, malicious litigation, and unreasonable pestering, and increase the intensity of punishment.

6. Effectively Strengthen Supervision of Case Filing

(1) Strengthen internal supervision. People's courts shall disclose case-filing procedures, standardize case-filing conduct, and strengthen supervision over the case-filing process. Higher-level people's courts shall fully exercise their supervisory functions through trial levels, and if a lower-level court fails to file cases that should be filed, it shall order it to promptly correct. If necessary, they may elevate the jurisdiction for trial or designate another lower-level court to accept and hear the case.

(2) Strengthen external supervision. People's courts shall consciously accept supervision. For issues and opinions fed back from the inspection of court case-filing registration work by people's congresses and their standing committees at various levels, they shall promptly propose corrective and implementation measures. For protests legally filed by the procuratorial organs against rulings not to accept, not to file, or to dismiss a case, they shall legally hear them. For procuratorial suggestions raised by the procuratorial organs, they shall promptly address them and provide a written reply. They shall consciously accept supervision from the news media and the people, promptly respond to reported and complained issues, and if problems indeed exist, shall legally correct them.

(3) Strengthen accountability. The supervision departments of the people's court shall intensify disciplinary supervision over case-filing work. If illegal acts such as failing to file cases that should be filed, delaying case filing, artificially controlling case filing, "not filing at the end of the year", or interfering with lawful case filing are discovered, the responsible persons and the relevant leading officials shall be seriously held accountable in accordance with laws and discipline. If the acts cause serious consequences or adverse social impact and constitute a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.

People's courts at all levels shall earnestly implement the spirit of these Opinions, effectively strengthen leadership, clarify responsibilities, make thorough arrangements, and carefully organize, to ensure the smooth progress of the reform of the case-filing registration system.
